pages.text: You were never alone out here. The others keep close and look after themselves: they root for food, pick up what is worth having, and pull a branch from a tree when they feel unsafe.

When something goes for you, they go for it. When you go for something, so do they - so choose what you anger.$(br2)Hold food, a weapon, anything, right-click one, press $(k:hominin_evolution.social) and choose $(l)Here, take this$(). Everything you say to a hominin goes through that menu now.

Call, and they call with you. One voice is a bluff; several is a reason to leave.$(br2)Right-click one to pick them out: they stop and face you, and the next $(k:hominin_evolution.social) speaks to them alone. $(k:sneak) and $(k:attack) to wrestle - play fighting is how fighting is learned.

Well fed and whole, they pair off and have children on their own, and tell you so. From habilis on a pair is a pair: one mate, kept. Every kind of hominin lives in a band of its own size, and the land will only feed so many.$(br2)If you die, the band does not. Nor, quite, do you.

There are other bands. They will not follow you, but they carry things.$(br2)Pick one out, press $(k:hominin_evolution.social) and choose $(l)Trade$(): you see everything they carry and what each thing is worth to them.

Press $(k:hominin_evolution.social) near your band to talk to them: to forage, to ask for food or a tool, or to say you are hurt. Near another band, ask them to walk with you for the day. Right-click one member first to talk to just them.
Stragglers find their way back to you.$(br2)Lose a whole band and some of what you learned is lost with it. Lose three, and your line ends.

$(l)Worth, to another band$()$(br)Everything falls into a tier. Trade for anything of the same tier or lower, never higher.$(br2)1 Common: food, sticks, rocks$(br)2 Useful: long branch, termite stick, quartzite$(br)3 Crafted: flake, Lomekwian core, chert$(br)4 Prized: chopper, spear

$(l)Treasured$()$(br)Top of the tiers: $(#b87333)obsidian$(), a $(#b87333)chert hammerstone$(), an $(#b87333)Oldowan multi tool$().$(br2)Worth is not fixed. Tools a band has never made are treasure to them; tools their ancestors made, they barely value.

Each of them carries nine things: two in the hands, seven more. Full up, they drop the least worth keeping for something better. They take out what the moment needs - a weapon when danger is near, a stick to dig or fish termites with, food in hand when hungry.$(br2)From habilis on, a big band splits into parties by day and comes together at night. Only those near you will come if you are attacked.

Frightened, the body decides: fight, stronger and harder to hurt, or flight, fast - up a tree, or later, back to the band. Sometimes it decides nothing, and they freeze until the band comes for them. It takes five minutes to happen again.

From habilis, they are their own people. Each favours a stone - chert, quartzite or basalt - and a few cannot leave obsidian alone, and will not hand it over for anything. They go out and break rocks on their own account, and they will tell you what they think of limestone.$(br2)Now and then one wants something, and says so, or offers you a trade for something you carry. Give them what they asked for, or their favourite food, and they remember it.

A member who is fond of you looks after you unasked: food when you are going hungry, a better weapon than the one you have, a hammerstone when you have none.$(br2)Right-click one and press $(k:hominin_evolution.social), then Info, to see who they are - sex, health, hunger, favourite foods, what they want, and how much they trust you.

Grooming is what holds a band together, and it costs the one thing that means anything: time. Right-click one of them, press $(k:hominin_evolution.social), then Groom, and stay beside them while you pick through their hair.$(br2)They do it to each other too, and on a hot day they will wade into a river to wash. By erectus there is too little hair left to pick, so it becomes cleaning instead - and one day, for sapiens, it becomes talk.

If the last of them dies, you do not simply carry on. Your chest closes, your eyes shut, and you come back to yourself ninety blocks away with a new band around you.$(br2)What you were stays where it happened, sitting with its head in its hands. Walk back and find it, and it will get up and come with you.

Close enough to someone (bond 3), you can live as them for a while: pick them out, then $(o)Become them$() under Together. You open your eyes where they stood; they carry on as you. Their info says when a mother is due, and nobody follows you in their sleep.

They talk among themselves, too. Stay near and you overhear it: what one of them is doing, what the band is building, the dark coming on, the season, the strangers over the ridge - and the other's answer. Something that has just happened - a birth, a death, a new roof, a kill - is talked over for a while after. Say something aloud and someone may have a word to add.

$(l)Negotiating$(), 4 to 0 - lower is better. You start at 2 or 1. Whoever near you talks best does the talking - at trades, gifts, offers for your ground - and a party talks as well as the best of it. A good talker gets a tier more in trades, more ground-worth when haggling, more for a gift. Good deals teach you. Some of the band are good at it; one kind of person is always flawless.

Tribe stats shows everyone's everything: knapping, hunting, talking, fighting, health, hunger, and what they are doing. $(l)Right-click a name$() to keep track of them - up to four, in the top right corner of the screen: which way, how far, how they are, what they are up to. Right-click again to stop.

They do what they say: talk of grubs and they have one; say they will find a stone and they come back with it. Sleep the night through and whoever was carrying has had the child by morning - sometimes two. Before erectus, a child rides on its mother's back.
When their hands are full and you give them something, they drop the least use of what they carry. When they carry more tools than they need and there is no pile, they ask you where it should be.

Others may walk this world too. Coming into it after them, you choose: walk with one of their bands - one of them, your blows pulled with theirs and theirs with yours - or make a band of your own, a long walk from anyone. Wherever they are, the others are on your map.

Lead a band with someone and you are both its leaders: what it needs, what other bands want of it, either of you hears and either of you can answer. And when a band evolves with others in the world, everyone has a few breaths to choose - go with it, split off, keep to their own, or join it. A band left behind is carried along, a little of its road already walked.

A brain is a great deal of food. Before erectus nobody will touch one; after, the hungry are drawn to them - and some carry the shaking sickness. When the band loses someone to it, it learns: we don't consume the flesh of the thought.
